questions: How do the access to multiple cosmological simulations and semi-analytic galaxy formation models influence the census of gaseous and stellar dust extinctions, gas-phase metallicities, star-formation rates, and stellar, gas, and dynamical masses derived from multi-Gaussian fitting of nebular emission lines and spectral energy distribution modeling?

What role does the inclusion of binary evolution pathways play in the stochasticity observed in galaxy parameters when comparing two-dimensional galaxy evolution models with one-dimensional models of smooth star formation?
What is the nature of the processes governing galaxy formation and evolution across different cosmic epochs?

How might the observations of LAEs at redshift z ~ 7.7 using the HAWK-I instrument at the VLT with a narrow band filter centred at 1.06 μm reveal insights into the fundamental characteristics of early galaxy formation?
Could the reliance on spectral energy distribution fitting solutions lead to a fundamental misunderstanding of the intrinsic properties of galaxies in the context of their formation and evolution?
